interpretations: For each examination with a matching patient, subtract the mean of nonmissing `aCL IgM` values across all matched examinations from that examination’s `aCL IgM`. Average these signed deviations within each exact `SEX` value, treating blank text as a group and excluding missing sex from group matches. Return the 10 examination entries whose deviation exceeds their sex group’s average, ordered by the excess descending with missing excesses last; show patient `ID`, `SEX`, `aCL IgM`, the deviation, and the excess, without rounding
queries:
WITH matched AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, e.`aCL IgM`
    FROM Examination AS e
    JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = e.ID
),
deviations AS (
    SELECT
        ID,
        SEX,
        `aCL IgM`,
        `aCL IgM` - AVG(`aCL IgM`) OVER () AS deviation
    FROM matched
),
sex_averages AS (
    SELECT SEX, AVG(deviation) AS average_deviation
    FROM deviations
    WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT
    d.ID,
    d.SEX,
    d.`aCL IgM`,
    d.deviation,
    d.deviation - s.average_deviation AS excess
FROM deviations AS d
JOIN sex_averages AS s ON d.SEX = s.SEX
WHERE d.deviation > s.average_deviation
ORDER BY excess IS NULL, excess DESC
LIMIT 10;
